rows.context:
[S1] (source=knowledge/guide, score=0.71, ref=resume_and_ats.md)
Resume And Ats - Raising an ATS match score: Mirror the exact wording of the job description where it is truthful (for example "Power BI" not just "BI tools"). Put a dedicated Skills section near the top. Use standard section titles: Summary, Skills, Experience, Projects, Education, Certifications. Save as a text-based PDF or DOCX, never a scanned image. Spell out acronyms once, e.g. "Natural Language Processing (NLP)". Do not keyword-stuff or add skills you cannot discuss in an interview; recruiters verify.

Order: contact line with LinkedIn/GitHub, 2-3 line summary targeted at the role, skills, experience or projects, education, certifications. Tailor the summary and the top skills for every application.

[S3] (source=knowledge/guide, score=0.59, ref=resume_and_ats.md)
Resume And Ats - How Applicant Tracking Systems work: An Applicant Tracking System (ATS) parses a resume into fields (contact, education, experience, skills) and ranks candidates by how closely their text matches the job description. Keyword overlap with the job description's required skills, job titles and tools is the strongest signal. Unusual layouts (tables, text boxes, multi-column designs, images, headers/footers) often break parsing, so key information can be lost before a human ever reads it.
